items.title: Equivalent characterizations of an element of the maximal ideal that cuts out the maximal ideal up to radical
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the equivalence of three conditions on an element f of the maximal ideal of a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring - that the maximal ideal is the radical of (f), that f lies in no minimal prime, and that A_f is the product of the localizations at the minimal primes - proves such an f exists, and, under the depth-one (for instance reduced) hypothesis, adds the equivalences with f being a nonzerodivisor and A_f being the total ring of fractions, and under reducedness further with A_f being the product of the residue fields at the minimal primes. The proof identifies the prime spectrum as the minimal primes together with the maximal ideal, derives the equivalence of (1) and (2) from the Zariski topology criterion, shows (2) implies (3) by describing Spec(A_f) as the finite discrete set of minimal primes and applying the dimension-zero structure theorem, and then treats the depth-one and reduced cases through associated primes and total rings of fractions (proof lines 8253-8291). H2: the assembly of these conditions is a real argument, with the identification of Spec(A_f) as the discrete set of minimal primes as its core.
